data.title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
data.authors: Wang J; Huang D; Liu B; Jiang W; Dang F; Chen L; Hou T; Yan P; Qi Y; Inuzuka H; Li L; Wei W

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human prostate cancer cell lines; mouse xenografts
data.finding: In human prostate cancer cells, the ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP degrades RICTOR; SPOP loss or cancer-derived SPOP mutations stabilise it, and the deubiquitinase USP8 opposes SPOP. A USP8 inhibitor lowered RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1 and suppressed tumour growth in mouse xenografts. Cell and xenograft work only; no human trial data.
data.abstract_excerpt: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3-based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression.
